def factor_tail_fragility_centered_asymmetry(df):
    """Drawdown-conditioned excess downside tail energy using causal EWMA estimates."""
    df_copy = df.copy()
    previous_close = df_copy["close"].shift(1)
    downside_tail = (previous_close - df_copy["low"]).clip(lower=0.0) / previous_close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    upside_tail = (df_copy["high"] - previous_close).clip(lower=0.0) / previous_close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    downside_energy = downside_tail.pow(2).ewm(span=30, min_periods=20, adjust=False).mean()
    upside_energy = upside_tail.pow(2).ewm(span=30, min_periods=20, adjust=False).mean()
    tail_imbalance = (downside_energy - upside_energy) / (downside_energy + upside_energy).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    drawdown = 1.0 - df_copy["close"] / df_copy["close"].rolling(60, min_periods=60).max().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    df_copy["factor_tail_fragility_centered_asymmetry"] = -tail_imbalance * drawdown
    return df_copy["factor_tail_fragility_centered_asymmetry"]
cross_sectional_rationale: The drawdown-conditioned tail imbalance is economically relative across contemporaneous stocks. Same-day ranking identifies the firms with the most downside-dominated tail stress while limiting market-wide variation in intraday excursion intensity.
